name: landing-05-workspace
prompt: Show another screen of this same landing page further down. Keep the identical thin top navigation bar (the S logo and "Smart-Clearance", the links, "Sign in" and the green "Book a demo" button) and the same visual system, fonts and miniature-diorama photography. Replace everything below the navigation; the hero, its headline, the big town and the giant carton must not appear. Below the navigation, on the pale sage-white ground: 1) A left-aligned heading in the heavy dark display type, "Your own workspace, set up for your supply chain.", with one line beneath: "Each manufacturer gets its own address, configured for how its stock really moves." 2) Across the middle, a surreal tilt-shift miniature scene: three small floating islands of Indian town, each carrying a different giant product package (a carton of snacks, a juice carton, a bottle of hair oil), joined by thin glowing green lines to one small green rounded-square S logo hovering in the centre. Under the first island a small white label "munchly.smartclearance.com · live" with a green dot; under the second and third, grey labels "your-company.smartclearance.com". 3) Under the scene, four white cards in a row with a small green icon, a bold title and one grey line: "Supply chain · one tap to approve a plan", "Finance · invoice, credit note and GST memo drafted", "Sustainability · a BRSR line an auditor can follow", "Distributors · nothing in their name without permission". 4) At the bottom, a row of small grey pill chips: "Distributor stock exports", "Tally", "BigQuery", "Google Workspace", "ExpireSoon", "GST e-invoice", "WhatsApp, soon". Miniature diorama photography for the islands; crisp flat interface for the navigation, text, cards and chips; all text legible.
postprocess: WebP; the PNG original stays local in .impeccable/mocks/
use: SC-25 design board: Section 'Your own workspace, set up for your supply chain': three floating islands of miniature town, each holding a giant product, tied by green lines to the Smart-Clearance mark; four cards for supply chain, finance, sustainability and distributors; a row of integration chips.
